decision.title: Union patterns keep one default priority, the lowest of their alternatives' (packet )

body.p: , after , , , , . No source change and no public header; one new unit test case.

item.p: Question (perf-15 found it): <xsl:template match="a[@n] | b"> with a later <xsl:template match="a">, applied to <r><a n="1"/><a/></r>, prints "plain plain" in sxml; XSLT 3.0 (6.5 of 3.0) makes the union one rule per alternative, a[@n] at 0.5, and gives "union plain".

What 4.0 says (the editor's draft of 28 October 2026, the same text as qtspecs master's specifications/xslt-40/src/xslt.xml): 6.4.1, "If the pattern is a UnionExprP then the default priority is the minimum of the default priorities of the alternatives", with a note calling it "a backwards incompatible change from XSLT 3.0 and earlier versions, which treated a template rule using a union pattern as equivalent to multiple template rules with different priorities"; a union rule is one rule, so next-match never runs it twice for an item both branches match. 6.4's changes list and the changes appendix (Issue 1770, PR 1772, 2025-02-11): "The default priority for a template rule using a union pattern has changed." 3.8.3 defines no difference for an effective version of 3.0, so version="3.0" gets the same answer. sxml already computes this (, sxml_xslt_pattern_compute_default_priority), and 's rule buckets put the one rule under both alternatives' kinds and names: the reproduction's "plain plain" is 4.0's answer. Nothing to change.

Reading taken (): 6.4 also says "The default priority of a pattern containing one or more predicates is +0.5"; read literally of the whole pattern it would make a[@n] | b 0.5 (and "union plain"). sxml reads it of a pattern whose own form has predicates (a predicated step, .[p]), with the union rule applied first, as 6.4.1's note requires: A | B "always has the same or lower priority as either alternative", and a branch's priority is "lowered to that of the other branch".

XT40 (the cases covering PR 1772): next-match-021a, -023a and -039a pass; next-match-025a and -026a (node()|element(x) against *:x) and conflict-resolution-1901a fail, as recorded: their expectations need the union above its lowest alternative (0.5 would give all three), against 6.4.1's text; the draft decides ().

Test: union_priority in tests/evaluator_template_test.c: the reproduction under versions 3.0 and 4.0 ("plain plain"), the union declared after a ("union plain": the tie at 0 goes to the later rule), node() | element(a) below *:a, and next-match from an item both branches match running the rule once. rule_buckets' comment cites 6.4.1.

Verified: debug-gcc and release, evaluator_template 10 of 10; clang-tidy clean. XT40 whole, base e4d928c2e and the change built alike (preset , snapshots), run one after the other on the same machine with TZ, LANG and LC_ALL unset, from each snapshot's root, sxml-xslt-test run --format=json (default catalog): 12,185 passed, 235 failed, 98 wrong error, 1,349 not run (13,867 cases) in both, 0 outcomes differ case by case; no gains (no source change). 7.30's suite (sxml-schematron-test run): 463 passed, 3 failed, 43 implementation-defined, 5 not applicable, as before; VEFA (run_vefa.py with the official EN 16931 UBL XSLT over the Invoice and CreditNote unit tests) 1,133 of 1,133 checks.
